whatItDoes: Wraps raster images (JPEG/PNG/WebP) as base64 inside SVG <image> elements sized to the source dimensions, so they can be embedded inline in HTML/CSS with vector scaffolding. Shows sanitized preview and allows download as .svg.
whyItExists: Embedding raster images as SVG is useful for inline HTML that needs a single file. Instead of linking, this creates a self-contained SVG that displays the raster via data URI, done locally without uploading.
whoShouldUse: Frontend developers needing inline SVG placeholders and designers wrapping photos for prototyping.
useCases: Embed a logo PNG as SVG for an email template that blocks external images
Wrap a screenshot as SVG to style it with CSS filters
Create an SVG data URI for a background-image without a separate file
instructions: Drop a JPEG/PNG/WebP image (10MB). The tool reads it as data URL and wraps it in <svg width/height viewBox><image href="data:..."/></svg>.
Preview the SVG (sanitized), copy the SVG code, or download as .svg. The image never leaves your browser.
examples: Input: 200×100 PNG → Output: <svg width="200" height="100" viewBox="0 0 200 100"><image href="data:image/png;base64,..." width="200" height="100"/></svg> (~50KB).
Input: WebP 800×600 → Output: SVG wrapper with same dims, viewBox 0 0 800 600, base64 data URI inside.
bestPractices: Use for small inline assets; large rasters as base64 bloat HTML — prefer for photos
Keep SVGs for icons and wrappers; for true vector, trace with a vectorizer instead
commonMistakes: Expecting vectorization — this wraps raster, not traces to paths
Embedding huge images — base64 adds 33% overhead; compress first with Image Compressor
faq: Is the image uploaded? No — wrapping is FileReader + string templating in your browser.
Is the SVG sanitized? Yes — preview is sanitized, output is plain <svg><image href="data:..."/> with no scripts.
Can I edit the SVG? Yes — download and open in any code editor; change width/height/viewBox as needed.
